newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean President Frei launches new subway line.
newsitem.headline: Chilean President Frei launches new subway line.

text.p: Chilean President Eduardo Frei officially opened on Saturday a $500 million extension of the Santiago subway, the largest public works project in the country in the last decade.

"This project...shows the institutional and professional capacity of the public sector to carry out large-scale schemes together with private companies," said Frei at the opening of the Bellavista station in the suburb of La Florida, the last stop on the line.
"This metro line must be one of the few in the world to finish on time and within budget."
The route, known as line five, is more than seven miles (12 km) long and has 12 stations along its track linking downtown Santiago and the city's southern suburbs.
After a welcoming ceremony at the Baquedano station in central Santiago, Frei, himself an engineer, drove a bright blue train through tunnels and over viaducts to La Florida.

He was accompanied by former president Patricio Aylwin, who authorised the project in 1991, and by French Transport, Housing and Tourism Minister Pierre-Andre Perissol. Paris granted preferential financing to buy trains and carriages, which were made in France.
The line, which is designed to carry 180,000 passengers a day, will help ease traffic congestion caused by the uncontrolled growth of La Florida over the last decade.
Commuters will now be able to travel to downtown Santiago in less than 20 minutes compared with over an hour in a bus -- the only other public transport available.
"This means a saving of more than $25 million in fuel and travelling time in 1997. It's a clear sign of progress and a better quality of life for people," said Frei.
Extending the metro is one of several projects planned by the government to upgrade Chile's antiquated infrastructure.
Much of the backlog is the result of the low level of investment in roads and railways under General Augusto Pinochet's military regime, which was in power from 1973-1990.
